items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: And he gave me a zero.

ctx.x: It must have prepared you pretty well for college studies?

Well it did. I was a very bad student. I mean I was goofing off, I was playing in the jazz band, I was drinking beer if I could ever put together ten cents for a beer I was running around and stuff. I managed to pass my courses by and large but yeah — although I didn’t realize it, I came to Hamilton better read than probably most of the kids. But also my father had been very involved in — he was an autodidact. He had run away from home when he was 16 from a good family up on Cohasset, Massachusetts. And he had…
You know on that kind of thing you’re either going to get an A or you’re going to get a zero.
